issues.legal_issue: An attachment made while a prior mortgage is subsisting reaches only the mortgagor’s equity of redemption, not the entire property.
material_facts: The owner had granted a simple mortgage over the property before the creditor obtained an attachment before judgment.
When the attachment was made, the mortgage remained subsisting and the owner retained the equity of redemption.
issues.conclusion: Only the owner’s equity of redemption could be attached; the attachment did not extend to the entire interest in the property.
issues.legal_principle: A prior subsisting mortgage limits the interest available for attachment to the mortgagor’s equity of redemption. The Court relied on the nature of the mortgage and the interests held by the mortgagor and mortgagee; it cited no earlier cases or statutory provision for this proposition.

predicates.money_claim_attachment: A creditor attaches property in connection with a claim for payment of money.
predicates.prior_mortgage_subsisting: A mortgage over the property was created before the attachment and remains in force when the attachment is made.
predicates.mortgagor_retains_equity_of_redemption: The owner of the property retains the right to redeem it when the attachment is made.

issues.definition: When a creditor attaches property for a money claim while a prior mortgage subsists and the owner retains the right to redeem, the attachment reaches only that right to redeem.

issues.legal_issue: A simple mortgagee without an interest in the equity of redemption cannot use a claim petition to object to attachment of that equity.
material_facts: The claimant held a simple mortgage created before the attachment and had no interest in the equity of redemption when the attachment was made.
The attachment concerned the mortgagor’s equity of redemption.
The claimant was not in possession of the property and filed a claim petition seeking to have the attachment raised.
issues.conclusion: The simple mortgagee was not entitled to file a claim petition objecting to attachment of the equity of redemption.
issues.legal_principle: Order 21 Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for adjudication of a claim or objection that attached property is not liable to attachment. The Court held that a simple mortgagee with no interest in the equity of redemption could not object to attachment of that interest. It cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: claim_petition_proceeding and simple_mortgagee and attachment_of_equity_of_redemption and mortgagee_has_no_equity_interest

predicates.claim_petition_proceeding: A claimant brings a proceeding to object to an attachment of property.
predicates.simple_mortgagee: The claimant holds a simple mortgage over the attached property.
predicates.attachment_of_equity_of_redemption: The attachment concerns the mortgagor’s equity of redemption rather than the mortgagee’s interest.
predicates.mortgagee_has_no_equity_interest: The mortgagee has no interest in the mortgagor’s equity of redemption.

issues.definition: A simple mortgagee who brings a claim petition against attachment of the equity of redemption but has no interest in that equity cannot object to the attachment.

issues.legal_issue: A creditor attaching mortgaged property can proceed only against the mortgagor’s equity of redemption, or against any sale proceeds remaining after satisfaction of the mortgage claim.
material_facts: The creditor obtained a money decree and sought to sell property that was subject to a prior mortgage.
After the attachment, the equity of redemption was sold in execution of the mortgage decree, and the mortgagee’s claim was to be satisfied from the sale price.
issues.conclusion: While the mortgage subsists, the attaching creditor may sell only the equity of redemption; if that interest has already been sold in execution of the mortgage decree, the creditor may proceed only against any balance remaining after the mortgagee’s claim is satisfied. The mortgagee’s right is not affected.
issues.legal_principle: An attachment made after a mortgage and while it subsists is subject to the mortgage. The attaching creditor may reach only the mortgagor’s equity of redemption, or any surplus from a sale of that equity after satisfaction of the mortgagee’s claim. The Court cited no statutory provision or earlier cases for this proposition.

predicates.money_decree_execution: A creditor seeks to enforce a money decree against property.
predicates.prior_mortgage_subsisting_at_attachment: A mortgage created before the attachment remains in force when the attachment is made.
predicates.attachment_of_mortgagor_interest: The attachment concerns an interest held by the mortgagor in the property.

issues.definition: In enforcement of a money decree, when an attachment concerns a mortgagor’s interest in property subject to a prior subsisting mortgage, the creditor can reach only that interest or any surplus remaining after the mortgage claim is satisfied.
